title: role velocity log - catalina
content:
Purpose: a compact running log to surface momentum (velocity) across role responsibilities, prioritized asks for my manager, and micro-experiments to nudge growth.

Quick thesis (one line): move from reactive ops to repeatable programs by converting 3 recurring fire-drills into 1 owned playbook + automation by Q4.

Signals I care about (signal bank):
- Time-to-resolve new-hire paperwork: baseline ~3 days (target <48h).
- Hiring funnel drop at offer->accept: current 8% drop (target <4%).
- 1:1 health: >80% of check-ins with defined next-action.
- Cross-team escalations reduced: track number of org-level escalations that require leadership sync.

Recent velocity (evidence snippets):
- 2025-09-30: Drafted consolidated new-hire checklist (removed 4 duplicate steps). Saved ~30m per hire (pilot n=6).
- 2025-11-04: Ran offer-package alignment session with Eng/Sales leads; updated compensation guideline doc (link in linked_artifacts). Feedback: fewer offer re-negotiations (anecdotal).
- 2025-12-08: Pilot of automated onboarding email reduced manual steps from 6 to 2 (observed on 5 hires).
- 2026-01-21: Cleaned backlog of pending access requests >7 days down from 17 -> 4 after new triage rule.

Open hypotheses & experiments (what to try and how I'll measure):
1) Hypothesis: Standardizing the hiring scorecard will speed decisions and reduce offer fallout. Metric: time from final interview to offer sent. Experiment: roll out to two hiring pods for 6 weeks and compare.
2) Hypothesis: A weekly "micro-doc" digest to hiring managers reduces ad-hoc questions. Metric: volume of Slack pings to #recruiting-help. Experiment: A/B by manager cohort.
3) Hypothesis: Document-level ownership reduces escalations. Metric: number of cross-org escalations per month.

Manager asks (ready-to-send, short):
- Ask 1: Block 90 minutes this month to decide on hiring-scorecard adoption across Eng and Product. I have pilot results + proposed template ready.
- Ask 2: Approval to convert two contracting approvals from manual to templated for Q2 (est. 6h/wk saved).
- Ask 3: Sponsor intro to Finance lead for headcount cadence alignment (one sync).

Prep cues for 1:1 (bullet script):
- 2-min: Quick data — hiring funnel status, recent wins (quantify).
- 6-min: Roadblock deep-dive — automated onboarding stuck because IT needs service account. Ask: decision/priority?
- 6-min: Manager asks (three bullets above).
- 6-min: Career pulse: want coaching on strategic influence and cross-org storytelling.
- 5-min: Agree next actions and deadlines.

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: Org changes deprioritize people-ops projects. Mitigation: package projects as "cost savings" or "time-to-productivity" and share early wins.
- Risk: Pilot noise (small n). Mitigation: run across two different teams to get variance.

Loose backlog (todo-style):
- Expand pilot new-hire checklist to full onboarding flow doc.
- Write success metric dashboard (simple sheet) for triage KPIs.
- Draft hiring-scorecard rollout comms.
- Create one-pager for Finance sync.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep evidence compact: 3 bullets per win, include date+metric.
- Ask succinctly: provide a single decision and the recommended option.
- Follow-ups: send meeting notes within 24h of sync.

One-line next-step (today): share final hiring-scorecard deck with manager + request 90-min decision slot.

Questions unresolved:
- Do we want hiring-scorecard enforced or advisory? Tradeoffs: enforcement reduces variance but may slow hiring for niche roles.
- How many teams willing to co-run the pilot? Need 2+ confirmed.

Quick links I refer to often (shorthand):
- Offer template: confluence:/people-ops/offer-template
- Onboarding checklist (pilot): confluence:/people-ops/onboarding-checklist-pilot
- Hiring cadence notes: confluence:/people-ops/hiring-cadence-2026

End of scratch.
